cards.existing: `Какой` (which/what kind) agrees with the noun: какой день, какая книга, какое окно, какие люди. Like an adjective in form.

cards.english: When does the performance start?
Can I pay by card?
cards.existing: Negative obligation: `не надо` (don't need) vs `нельзя` (forbidden). Big difference: `не надо` = it's unnecessary, `нельзя` = it's not allowed.

cards.english: What building is that?
cards.existing: Question words start the sentence: кто (who), что (what), где (where), когда (when), почему (why), как (how), сколько (how much), куда (where to), откуда (from where).

cards.english: I don't speak Russian.
I don't understand anything.
They don't have children.
cards.existing: Pronouns after `у`: меня/тебя/него/неё/нас/вас/них (genitive forms). `У него` (he has), `у неё` (she has). The owner is in genitive.

cards.english: When will you return home?
Where does this road lead?
cards.existing: `Какой` (which/what kind) agrees with the noun: какой день, какая книга, какое окно, какие люди. Like an adjective in form.

cards.english: What a beautiful building!
The nurse runs every morning.
cards.existing: Walking vs vehicle: `идти (idti)/ходить` for on foot, `ехать/ездить` for any vehicle. Russian distinguishes how you move, English doesn't.

cards.english: I am thirty-two years old.
cards.existing: Counterintuitive for English: 'two houses' isn't `два домы` – it's `два дома` (gen sg). Numbers force this case shift.

cards.english: She is twenty-one years old.
She is thirty-two years old.
cards.existing: Compound numbers ending in 2/3/4 still take genitive singular: `двадцать два года` (dvadtsat' dva goda) (22 years), `тридцать три рубля` (33 rubles). 22/23/24/32/33/34… all behave like bare 2/3/4.

cards.english: The salesman often cooks lunch.
What a quiet morning!
How long is the trip?
The doctor usually listens to music.
What is the name of this street?
I have no reason to go there.
cards.existing: Add prefixes for more nuance: `при-` (arrive), `у-` (leave), `пере-` (cross), `до-` (reach). `Прихожу домой` (I arrive home), `ухожу` (I leave).

cards.english: Until tomorrow, have a good evening.
Six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
What is your shoe size?
What happened to your car?
cards.existing: After `с` (with), the noun goes instrumental: `с братом`, `с сестрой`, `с друзьями`. Without `с`, instrumental marks the instrument itself.

cards.english: I don't have free time.
Grandmother washes dishes before bed.
Mom calls grandma every evening.
cards.existing: Frequency adverbs `всегда` (always), `никогда` (never) don't change shape. They sit before the verb: `я всегда читаю`.

cards.english: Grandmother has many interesting stories.
One plus one equals two.
Dad cooks lunch every day.
cards.existing: `Никогда не` (Nikogda ne) – Russian doubles up on negatives. `Я никогда не был там` (I never not have-been there). Don't drop the `не`; it's required.

cards.english: Where are you going on vacation?
Mom paints a picture every day.
cards.existing: `Весь (Ves)/вся/всё/все` covers 'all', 'the whole', 'everyone', 'everything' depending on form. Context + ending tells you which.

cards.english: The flight takes about three hours.
Hello, is this seat free?
The boy often works in the office.
The girl paints a picture every day.
cards.existing: `Каждый` (every) and `весь` (all/whole) act like adjectives – match gender, number, case. `Каждый день` (m, nom), `всю ночь` (f, acc).

cards.english: There was a serious conversation yesterday evening.

cards.english: We have never been late for work.

cards.existing: Motion verbs come in pairs. Unidirectional (идти (idti), ехать) for one trip in progress. Multidirectional (ходить, ездить) for round trips / habits.

cards.english: Could you tell me where the metro is?

cards.existing: `Много`, `мало`, `сколько`, `несколько` (much, little, how many, several) all take genitive plural: `много книг`, `мало времени`.

cards.english: The new house was built in half a year.

cards.existing: `Если + future tense` for real conditions: `Если будет дождь, я останусь дома` (If it rains, I'll stay home). Both halves go in future.

cards.existing: `Свой` (one's own) refers back to the subject, regardless of person. `Он любит свою жену` (he loves his [own] wife). Use `свой` when subject = owner.
